entries.note: Shimamura 2012 (PMID 22806877) resolves; quote verbatim in abstract. Untested at model opening is right. Proia 2012 (Jan) and Graham 2012 (Feb) precede it in the same year; Garon 2013 (luminespib NSCLC xenografts) also belongs to this panel.

Sessa 2013 resolves; PBMC HSP70 and tumour client depletion moved at RP2D, abstract only. Goldman 2013 (epub 2013-03-25, same drug as the model) is the earlier same-year source. product_in_model false here but true on the identical dose pairing; harmonise.
Shimamura 2012 quote verbatim; regimen prediction (tumour t1/2 58 h supports weekly dosing) stated before any human comparison; untested correct.

Decision 4 case 3: Sessa states xenograft-active concentrations reached at 70 mg/m2, single-agent NSCLC failed, so contra derived_from efficacy, counted once. Sessa's stated comparison is to luminespib xenografts (Garon 2013), not Shimamura; product_in_model should match engagement entry 2.
Shimamura 2012 quote verbatim; EGFR and ERBB2 subsets named before the phase 2 read out; untested correct.

Socinski 2013 resolves; both quotes verbatim; registry confirms primary endpoint PFS at 16 weeks, no posted results. Predicted EGFR-mutant effect absent (0 of 15 PR, 13.3% PFS16); all PRs ALK in cohort C. Patient-level contra supported.

Sang 2013 (epub 2013-03-26) quote verbatim. Synta's ASCO 2011 release and 8-K (June 2011) had already reported four ALK objective responses, so the model followed the patient result: retro under decision 10, own track.

Status holds (registry results 2016-07-01; Pillai 2020 verbatim; stopped for futility). Synta press release 2015-10-20 (tier 5) announced the futility termination; decision 7 takes the earliest admissible source, so year 2015 with the tier 3/1 record setting status.

Piotrowska 2018 quotes verbatim; registry results 2018-04-10; primary ORR with a 20% PR+SD>=3 mo bar, met (38%). Jorge 2018 (epub 2018-08-28) post-dates the trial it calls confirmatory; not a retrodiction by decision 10, but model_first_use_year 2018 understates (trial started 2013 on this model).
Ying 2012 (epub 2011-12-05) quote verbatim; an efficacy paper's claim of no cardiac or liver toxicity; untested at opening is correct.

Goldman 2013 quote verbatim. The stated no-cardiac/liver prediction held, but the model was silent on diarrhoea, the DLT and commonest AE (78% in Socinski 2013), a harm measurable in mice: askable silence contradicted is contra under decision 4.
entries.adjudication_note: RULE QUESTION: does an efficacy paper's incidental no-cardiac/liver claim make it a safety model whose silence on mouse-measurable GI toxicity is askable (decision 4: #54 'relied on for that question' vs #89 species test)? Stated prediction held; kept same.

entries.note: Zhou 2013 resolves; quote verbatim. The abstract opens by stating the clinical ocular split the rats then reproduced, so retro under decision 10. Felip 2018 visual disorders and Piotrowska 2018 (76% visual changes) are the patient side.

Kanamaru 2014 (PMID 24418710; J Toxicol Sci 39:59, print Feb 2014, no epub) resolves; quote verbatim in the abstract. Opening untested at first class use, publication-year proxy, model entry first in a same-year collision (#30). Correct.
entries.detail: Dogs were dosed with Chugai CH5164840 and CH5449302, same-mechanism siblings outside the member list; the drafter brief allows sibling dosing with product_in_model false, and the rule-12 'other' case (#69) is a sibling class (anti-PD-L1 for anti-PD-1), not a sibling drug of the same mechanism. prediction_level class is right: the question is whether HSP90 inhibition causes retinal toxicity, not which patients. The run date of the dog studies is not public; 2014 is a proxy, allowed under decision 7 (#112).

entries.note: Quote verbatim (39-word fragment of the abstract's penultimate sentence). The paper interprets the dog retinopathy against already-reported clinical visual disorders, so retro under decision 10, never same. Class-level, comparison_stated true at low resolution, year 2014 correct.
entries.detail: Decision 10 and the drafter brief: a model built or run after the clinic knew the answer is a retrodiction. Clinical visual disorders on HSP90 inhibitors (luminespib phase 1, ESMO 2010 / Sessa 2013) predate the Feb 2014 paper, and the abstract's own sentence puts the dogs beside 'some clinical trials of Hsp90 inhibitors', so comparison_stated true and source_calls_it match are supported. No member drug was dosed; the member-drug patient side is luminespib (Felip 2018 visual disorders 79.7%, Piotrowska 2018 76%), which matches the direction, so retro rather than contra. The rat track (Zhou 2013, safety 3) is a different species and readout, so a separate model_id is right. Note the dog track carries an opening untested entry in the same year while the rat track does not; that is a consistency point for the existing verdict, not an error here.

entries.note: De Raedt 2011 (PMID 21907929; Cancer Cell 20:400, print Sept 2011, Crossref created 2011-09-10, no online-first) resolves; quote verbatim in abstract; PMC3233475 full text confirms 'none of the single agents ... exerted a cytotoxic response'. Opening untested at 2011 correct.
entries.detail: IPI-504 (retaspimycin) is outside the member list, so product_in_model false is right. Own track is justified: an autochthonous Kras G12D; p53-deficient GEMM whose single-agent call (no regression) is the opposite of the xenograft panel's (Acquaviva 2012). prediction_level patient follows the tile's convention for genotype-defined predictions (efficacy 2 was checked as patient-level contra).

entries.note: Socinski 2013 (PMID 23553849, epub 2013-04-03) quotes verbatim; cohort B is KRAS. Same holds under #58: the GEMM stated the monotherapy null as a prediction and was discriminating (combination regressed). Not retro: the paper never mentions ganetespib or NCT01031225.
entries.detail: The question put to this check: is a no-effect prediction confirmed by a null cohort same or untested? Decision 4 as decided (RULES_V3_PROPOSAL §4, #58): a null-null is same only when the model made the null a prediction; the #58 recommendation adds that the null must be discriminating (falsifiable). Both hold here. De Raedt states the single-agent null as a result ('none of the single agents investigated in this study exerted a cytotoxic response when administered individually') and draws the clinical inference that such agents 'might be overlooked if they are assessed exclusively as mono-therapies'; and the same MRI system showed regression on IPI-504 plus rapamycin, so a ganetespib monotherapy response in KRAS-mutant patients would have contradicted it (#10). So same, direction_only, not untested. Retrodiction checked, since the drafter left it open: Synta's 8-K exhibit 99.1 of 2011-06-04 did report cohort B (13 evaluable, 5/13 SD, no objective response, headlined as 62% target-lesion shrinkage), three months before De Raedt's print date; but decision 10 requires post-dates AND motivated by, and the paper is an Nf1/MPNST and Kras lung mechanism study of Infinity's IPI-504 that never names ganetespib or the trial, with no online-first and a Sept 2011 print, so the experiments were not run to reproduce the cohort. The public reading in June 2011 was encouraging, not a null; the clean null (0/17 PR, 5.9% PFS16) is Socinski 2013, the entry's year. The GEMM's positive (combination) prediction was tested in NSCLC only with retaspimycin plus everolimus (NCT01427946, started 2011-07, no posted results), outside the member list, so the drafter's 'only the monotherapy half is scored' is right. Confidence low is appropriate: own pairing, sibling drug in the model, p53 status of cohort B unknown.

missing: Kanamaru 2014, 'Retinal toxicity induced by small-molecule Hsp90 inhibitors in beagle dogs', J Toxicol Sci 39:59, doi:10.2131/jts.39.59 (PMID 24418710): a second animal retinal-toxicity model (dog ERG and photoreceptor histology) compared with the class's clinical visual disorders; dosed with non-member Chugai inhibitors CH5164840/CH5449302, so a sibling-drug track (product_in_model false) or out of class under decision 12; post-dates the clinic, so retro at best.

Garon 2013, 'The HSP90 inhibitor NVP-AUY922 potently inhibits non-small cell lung cancer growth', Mol Cancer Ther, doi:10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-12-0998 (PMID 23493311): luminespib's own NSCLC cell-line and xenograft work; same nsclc-xenograft-panel track, but the proper model_src for the Sessa 2013 pairings (engagement 2, dose 2) rather than the ganetespib paper.

Acquaviva 2012, 'Targeting KRAS-mutant non-small cell lung cancer with the Hsp90 inhibitor ganetespib', Mol Cancer Ther, doi:10.1158/1535-7163.MCT-12-0615 (PMID 23012248): the panel's KRAS-mutant prediction; Socinski 2013 cohort B (KRAS) 5.9% PFS at 16 weeks with no responses is a second patient-level miss on the same track, worth naming in efficacy entry 2.

Synta press release 2015-10-20, 'Synta Announces Termination for Futility of Ganetespib Phase 3 GALAXY-2 Trial in Lung Cancer' (https://ir.madrigalpharma.com/node/8606; also filed on Form 8-K): tier-5 patient-side report of the GALAXY-2 failure nine months before the registry posting; sets the date of efficacy entry 4.

Synta 8-K exhibit 99.1, June 2011 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1157601/000110465911033406/a11-14314_1ex99d1.htm): ASCO 2011 report of ALK-rearranged responses to ganetespib (six of eight with shrinkage, four objective responses); dates the patient result the Sang 2013 ALK model retrodicted.
rule_questions: Dating (decision 7): when a tier-5 press release reports a trial failure nine months before the tier-3 registry posting (GALAXY-2: 2015-10-20 vs 2016-07-01), does the press release set `year` while the higher-tier record sets the status, or is `year` limited to the sources that can set status?

Decision 10 boundary: a model whose published report (Jorge 2018, epub 2018-08-28) post-dates the registry results of the trial it motivated (NCT01854034, started 2013, results 2018-04-10). Not 'motivated by the patient result', so not a retrodiction, but no public model source pre-dates the trial. Prospective `same`, and is `model_first_use_year` the trial start (2013, proxy) or the model's epub (2018)?
`model_kind` has no value for cell-line or Ba/F3-only models; the draft used `animal` for the exon-20 track. Which value is intended?

Safety (decision 4): does an efficacy paper's incidental claim ('no evidence of cardiac or liver toxicity', Ying 2012) constitute a safety model whose silence on GI toxicity is 'askable', or is only a toxicology study's silence scored? The safety-2 correction rests on the first reading.

Decision 12 for safety models dosed only with non-member drugs of the same mechanism (Kanamaru 2014 dog retina, Chugai HSP90 inhibitors): a sibling-drug track with `product_in_model: false`, or outside the class?

Decision 4 (#58) for efficacy: the decided text requires only that 'the model made the null a prediction'; the #58 recommendation also asks that the null be discriminating. The GEMM (De Raedt 2011) meets both, so efficacy 7 is same; confirm that a sibling-drug (IPI-504) monotherapy null transfers to a member (ganetespib) on the same terms as a positive sibling prediction (product_in_model false).

Decision 10 wording: the rule says 'post-dates and is motivated by the patient result'; the models-check task says 'run after the patient result was known'. For efficacy 7 the KRAS interim (Synta 8-K 2011-06-04) preceded De Raedt's print (2011-09) but the paper never names the drug or trial. Scored under the decided (motivated-by) text; if the stricter gloss is adopted, the entry needs the experiment run date, which is not public.
